consensus_summary: Biblical peace (shalom/eirēnē) is comprehensive wholeness and right relationship, chiefly reconciliation with God through Christ, rather than mere absence of conflict; inner calm, social peacemaking, fruit of the Spirit, and eschatological harmony are complementary facets, with a recognized counter-theme of false peace.
book_summary: Covenant wholeness restored through righteousness—completion, restoration, and repayment—rather than merely a truce or feeling; counterfeit peace announces wholeness over an unkept covenant; opposite is sword.
consensus_core_identification: restored wholeness/reconciliation with God (shalom realized in Christ)
boundary_disagreement: Book conditions true peace strictly on covenant righteousness (completion/repayment) and treats undeclared truce or mere feeling as non-peace or counterfeit; consensus admits inner tranquility and social dimensions as valid complementary cases without always requiring explicit covenant-righteousness framing.
rationale: Both cores identify the same general referent—restorative wholeness beyond cessation of hostilities—and both flag false peace. The book preserves that category but materially tightens conditions and precision by centering the mechanism on righteousness under covenant and by sharper exclusion of truce/feeling, thereby narrowing the cases covered relative to the broader multi-facet consensus while remaining compatible at the center.
strongest_objection: Consensus primaries foreground Christ’s reconciling person and work as the definitional center; the book’s gloss foregrounds the righteousness-covenant mechanism and only alludes to Christ via citations.
